scope: SEC Form 8-K filings carrying structured item code 2.05 (Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities) whose text states an absolute count of employees, positions or roles to be reduced.
assembled_by: Claude Code session, single actor. This manifest has NOT been through the three-actor transcription/matching/publication review chain that docs/RECALL_BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md requires before a recall number may be posted to /benchmarks/recall, and it is therefore NOT published there.
how_it_was_assembled: 1. ENUMERATION. EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index), forms=8-K, one calendar month per request across 2025-07-01..2026-06-30, query '"Item 2.05"'. A hit was kept only when the response's STRUCTURED `items` array contains "2.05" — the code the filer put in the SGML header, not a text match. 215 distinct accessions.

2. ENUMERATION CONTROL. The same twelve months were pulled again with the independent query '"exit or disposal activities"'. It returned ZERO item-2.05 accessions that the first query missed, in every month. Two further controls over 2026-05..06 ('"Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities"' and a disjunction) also added nothing. That is the evidence the enumeration is effectively complete for the window; it is not a proof.

3. TRANSCRIPTION. Every document in each filing (primary 8-K plus exhibits, up to six files) was fetched from www.sec.gov/Archives and tag-stripped. Sentences containing both a number and an employee noun were extracted, and each of the 64 filings with such a sentence was read by hand.

4. ADJUDICATION. A filing enters the gold set only when it states an ABSOLUTE count of affected employees/positions/roles. Five were excluded for stating only a percentage, a retained headcount or a pre-action total, which is the same thing extractor.py's _percent_only_mention / _count_in_text guards reject — including them would score a documented design decision as a miss. Two accessions are the same announcement filed twice and were collapsed. Counts follow the tracker's own reading rules (range -> lower bound, 'up to N' -> N).

5. MATCHING. For each event, the live public /query API was asked for the employer by the aliases recorded below, all of which come from the FILING (filer name, or an operating subsidiary the filing names) and never from a tracker lookup. A tracker row counts only when its company name token-PREFIX-matches an alias (so Xperi does not match Experian, Gemini does not match Capgemini, Sight Sciences does not match Insight Behavioral) and its date falls in [filing_date-90d, filing_date+270d]. Every candidate was then read by an editor and a per-row decision recorded below.

6. RE-MEASUREMENT CONTRACT. Only events the editor decided `matched` count in the numerator when this set is re-run; the denominator stays 57. An event the editor decided `not_matched` whose candidate rows are recorded in `rejected_candidate_event_ids` stays silent. Any OTHER row that newly satisfies the alias/window rule for a not-matched event is reported as a candidate needing adjudication and is NOT counted — a machine must not promote its own recall by finding a row an editor has not looked at.
why_this_is_independent: The set is enumerated from the filer's own structured item code in SEC EDGAR, a primary regulator index. No row was selected by searching this tracker, no aggregator or third-party layoff list was consulted, and the selection rule was fixed before any tracker query. It is NOT independent of the tracker's DESIGN: the tracker already runs an EDGAR collector over the same corpus, so this measures whether the pipeline actually captures what its own primary source publishes.
what_it_can_and_cannot_support: n=57. At 24 matched the Wilson 95% interval is roughly [30%, 55%] — a range, not a point. It supports 'well under half' and it does not support any figure to the nearest percent. It describes ONE source family (US public companies filing Item 2.05 with an explicit count) over ONE twelve-month window. It says nothing about private employers, non-US employers, WARN-only events, or news-only events, and it must never be quoted as 'the tracker's recall'.

matching_rule.company_match: token-prefix on the normalised company name after dropping corporate suffixes (inc, corp, co, company, ltd, limited, llc, lp, plc, nv, sa, se, ag, the, holdings, holding)
matching_rule.unreachable_policy: An event whose query could not be completed is UNKNOWN, never a miss. Above the unreachable ceiling the whole measurement is UNKNOWN — a host outage must not manufacture a recall regression.
matching_rule.numerator: events whose match_decision is 'matched' and which are still findable by the alias/window rule. Denominator is every reference event.

excluded_filings.count_evidence: PERCENT/REMAINDER ONLY: the only figure is the REMAINING core workforce ('end the year with a core workforce of about 75,000 employees'). No absolute cut count is stated, so extractor.py would reject it too.
PERCENT/REMAINDER ONLY: cut is 'approximately 29% of its current employees'; the only absolute figure (15) is the RETAINED headcount.
PERCENT/TOTAL ONLY: cut is 'approximately one-third of its current approximately 260 employees'; 260 is the PRE-cut total.
AMBIGUOUS: 'personnel-related costs to sever or retain approximately 200 to 300 employees' does not isolate how many are severed.
PERCENT ONLY: 'reduce ... by approximately 85%, from 57 full-time employees to 9'. The cut (48) is derivable but never stated; extractor.py forbids a derived count.
